topics.label: Lecture opening and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the session's themes and outlines the learning outcomes for cancer cell genetics and transformation.

topics.label: Tumor viruses, cellular oncogenes, and transformation assays
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how the study of transforming retroviruses revealed normal cellular genes that drive cancer and established laboratory assays to measure cell transformation.

topics.label: Oncogene and tumor suppressor gene functions and mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics define the classes of cancer-driving mutations and explain how oncogenes and tumor suppressor genes alter regulatory pathways and cellular phenotypes.

topics.label: Molecular mechanisms of sequence and chromosomal instability
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how failures in DNA replication, repair mechanisms, and chromosome segregation during mitosis generate genetic instability in cancer cells.

topics.label: Multi-step tumor progression and hereditary cancer predisposition
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how sequential somatic mutations and inherited genetic defects drive cancer progression over time.

topics.label: Closing remarks and recommended reading
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the lecture with recommended reading and outlines the topic of the next session.
